newsitem.title: UK: British anti-gun song may be Christmas bestseller.
newsitem.headline: British anti-gun song may be Christmas bestseller.

text.p: A Bob Dylan song with an extra verse calling for a ban on handguns and backing vocals by children from Dunblane in Scotland looks set to become the best-selling record in Britain this Christmas.

Dunblane is the town where a crazed gunman killed 16 schoolchildren and their teacher in March. Brothers and sisters of the dead children sing backing vocals on the recording of the American singer's "Knockin' on Heaven's Door'.
The record goes on sale on December 9 and has already logged advance orders of nearly half a million, Jeremy Marsh of the BMG record company told a news conference on Thursday.
The group is mainly made up of local musicians, lent weight by guitarist Mark Knopfler of the top-selling band Dire Straits.
Dylan, apparently for the first time, has given the producers permission to insert an extra verse into the song:
"Lord, these guns have caused too much pain,
This town will never be the same,
So, for the bairns (children) of Dunblane,
The British government introduced new gun controls after the massacre but resisted the total ban on handguns wanted by the parents of the murdered children.
John Crozier, one of those parents, declined to comment on the government's position at the news conference, but said he hoped the song would "contribute to reducing the gun culture".
"We particularly hope parents will buy the record, rather than toy guns, for their children at Christmas," he added.
The record cover features a picture of a smiling clown drawn by Crozier's daughter, Emma, who was five when she was killed.
Bookmakers William Hill is taking bets on the best-selling record this Christmas, but is declining wagers on the Dunblane single as "inappropriate for a light-hearted, fun bet".
If the song is the Christmas "number one", it will pay out on the runner-up.
